findings.issue: The subtitle-lift alignment is guarded only by a dev-time test. There is no runtime invariant check. Verified in code: both sides of the pairing swallow a length mismatch silently — `_llm_common._build_user_message` does `except StopIteration: break` (encode side) and `_patch_text_with_ru_paragraphs` does `except StopIteration: pass` (decode side). A divergence therefore raises nothing, logs nothing, and alerts nothing; it publishes the last paragraph in English and/or bolds the wrong spans. The spec's constraint 'снимать первый элемент нужно из обоих списков одновременно' plus 'тест-сторож на равенство длин' (Risk 3) only covers fixtures the developer thought to write. The live divergence source is different: `filter_blocks` runs over the block list and `filter_boilerplate` runs over the derived flat list — two separate passes over two separate lists, both before the lift in t-hunted (order is marked CRITICAL at t_hunted_source.py:201-204). Any live article where those two filters disagree on one entry breaks parity regardless of how carefully the lift is coded.
findings.why_matters: This is the spec's own headline trap (the 2026-05-06 incident) and the mitigation does not cover the case that actually caused it in prod. orangetrack solved it structurally (`subtitle = ""` hardcoded, orangetrack_source.py:808); t-hunted/lamley are being given the fragile version instead, on the two sources that carry the most posts. The failure mode is silent English text in a published article — exactly what the operator would not catch until a subscriber does.
findings.fix: Add a requirement to «Как должно работать» / «Ограничения»: the parser must verify, at runtime, that the number of patchable blocks (paragraph/lead/heading/list_item) equals `len(paragraphs)` before returning; on mismatch it drops `blocks` and returns the flat result, and logs a WARNING. This is the same fail-open rule the spec already demands in AC6 — state that a count mismatch counts as «сбой разбора разметки», because it is not an exception and no try/except will catch it. Add an AC: «расхождение числа блоков и абзацев → статья выходит плоским текстом, а не с рассинхроном».

findings.issue: The spec says nothing about images, but switching a source from the flat path to the blocks path silently changes image rendering on every single post. Verified in telegraph_publisher.py: `_build_content` (flat) places the first image as hero and then interleaves one image every 3rd paragraph, capped by the parser's limit (t_hunted_source.py:49 `_IMAGE_LIMIT = 30`, lamley_source.py:93 `IMAGE_LIMIT = 10`). `_build_content_from_blocks` (blocks) renders every image block at its DOM position with NO cap at all — and when `blocks` is non-empty the `images` list is ignored entirely, so the parser's limit becomes dead code for that source. t-hunted is a Blogger photo-gallery blog (the limit is 30 precisely because posts run long).
findings.why_matters: Two distinct production effects on 100% of t-hunted and lamley posts from the first tick after deploy: (1) layout changes — images land wherever the Blogger DOM puts them rather than in the every-3rd-paragraph rhythm the channel has used to date; (2) the image cap disappears — a gallery post that used to publish 30 images can now publish all of them, growing the Telegraph page without bound. Neither is mentioned in «Как должно работать», the ACs, «Ограничения» or «Риски», so nobody will decide it deliberately and the operator meets it live.
findings.fix: Decide and record in the spec: does the image cap still apply on the blocks path (cap the number of `image` blocks in the parser), and is DOM-position placement the wanted look for photo-gallery posts? Add an AC covering it, e.g. «число картинок в публикации не превышает прежний предел источника (t-hunted 30, lamley 10)», and add the layout change to «Ограничения» so the operator's post-deploy сверка explicitly checks image placement, not just bold/headings.

findings.issue:
AC4, AC5 and AC6 cannot all hold on the flat (no-blocks) path, and the spec does not say which wins. AC4 requires literal `**` to be gone «включая статьи вообще без разметки, где маркеры добавила сама LLM». AC5 requires LLM-added bold to be rendered as bold, not cut. On an article with no `blocks` there is no container for `runs` — `telegraph_publisher._build_content` emits plain `

` strings only, and there is no path from a flat paragraph to ``. So on that path the two ACs demand opposite things. AC6 makes this path permanent, not hypothetical: fail-open on a parse failure produces exactly a no-blocks article, and articles already sitting in the queue at deploy time are no-blocks too (interview: «очередь разгребается за 1-2 дня»).
findings.why_matters: The implementer must choose: strip the markers (AC4 satisfied, AC5 violated on this path) or synthesize `blocks` from the flat paragraphs when markers come back (AC4 and AC5 satisfied, but AC6's «статья публикуется обычным текстом» is no longer literally true and the fail-open path grows new behaviour). Both are defensible and they produce visibly different pages. Leaving it unstated means a product decision is made silently inside a tech-spec.
findings.fix: State the rule for the no-blocks path explicitly in «Как должно работать» and reword the affected AC. Recommended: markers on a no-blocks article are decoded into real bold by synthesizing minimal blocks from the flat paragraphs (satisfies both AC4 and AC5 uniformly, and gives the same answer on every path); if that is rejected, say plainly in AC5 that LLM-added bold is honoured only when the article carries blocks and is stripped otherwise.

findings.issue: No kill switch and no rollback plan, on a change that alters the visible output of every post from four sources at once. The spec's only operational note is «Деплой — вне окна публикаций 10:00–20:00 МСК». That constraint cuts both ways: if the first post of the day at 10:00 looks wrong, redeploying to fix it is exactly what the constraint forbids, so the bad rendering rides through all three slots (10:00 / 15:00 / 19:30) until 20:00. The project already has the pattern for this — `REVIEW_BUTTONS_ENABLED` (fail-closed) and `DEDUP_SERIES_ENABLED` are env-gated rollouts of comparable output-affecting features — and the spec does not reuse it.
findings.why_matters: The spec's own acceptance procedure is «взять 3–5 свежих статей с каждого источника после деплоя и сверить» — i.e. verification happens only after real posts have gone out. Without a switch there is nothing to do when that сверка fails, and no way to stage the rollout source by source (turn on t-hunted, verify, then lamley) which is what the verification plan implicitly assumes.
findings.fix: Add to «Ограничения» a per-source (or at minimum global) env flag that turns block emission off and returns the source to today's flat behaviour without a code change, defaulting to the state the operator wants for the first day. Add an AC: «флаг выключен → источник публикуется в точности как до фичи». Add a rollback sentence to «Как проверить» describing what the operator does if сверка fails inside the publish window.

findings.issue: «Переиспользовать обходчик разметки orangetrack» contradicts «orangetrack трогать нельзя» (AC9 + «Ограничения»). Code research quantifies why: `_runs_from_tag` + `_safe_href` + `_safe_img_src` + `_INLINE_FORMAT_TAGS` (~190 lines) are importable as-is, but `_walk` — the part that actually turns a DOM into blocks — is a closure over `blocks`/`seen_image_bases` inside `_parse_content_encoded` and is not importable at all. Making it reusable requires editing orangetrack_source.py. The spec's wording therefore permits only the interpretation the spec's own Risk 1 argues against: copy-paste the walker into three more files.
findings.why_matters: Risk 1's mitigation (hotfix a509722, verified present in git, fixes the bold-bleed, the double-space join via `_text_from_runs`, and the preview allowlist) works exactly once. If the code is copied rather than shared, the next defect propagates across five files again and the hotfix's value evaporates. Conversely, if the implementer reads «трогать нельзя» literally, autoevolution keeps its strictly weaker duplicate `_runs_from_tag` (no `formats` support at all) and the codebase ends up with three divergent copies of one contract.
findings.fix: Replace the ambiguous decision with an explicit one: extraction of the shared walker into a common module IS in scope, orangetrack is refactored to consume it, and «orangetrack трогать нельзя» is restated as what it actually means — orangetrack's PUBLISHED OUTPUT must stay byte-identical, pinned by its existing 94 tests. Note separately that autoevolution's work is different in kind and much smaller (swap its weaker `_runs_from_tag` for the shared one; `_scrape_article_page` is ~0% reusable and is not being rewritten).

findings.issue: Including mattel is scope padding. The source is commented out in `news_bot.SOURCES`, and the rationale in the code (news_bot.py:3540-3547) states that corporate.mattel.com moved to Astro/Netlify, the body renders client-side, «за всю историю Mattel выдал ноль Hot Wheels статей», and — decisively — that restoring it «потребует... переписав парсер под новый API». The spec's justification is «когда оператор его включит, всё уже будет готово», which the project's own comment contradicts: the parser will be rewritten when/if mattel returns, so formatting work done now is thrown away.
findings.why_matters: Mattel is roughly a quarter of the surface for zero live benefit: 42 existing tests to keep green, four exact-equality assertions to consciously update, plus spec-level decisions unique to it (its `find_all` includes `h1` and excludes `blockquote`, and its empty-body case forces a `blocks = []` vs `blocks = None` decision). It also cannot be verified: the spec's primary success criterion is pairwise comparison against 3-5 fresh live articles, and a disabled source that has never produced one makes that impossible.
findings.fix: Cut mattel from scope and record it in «Технические решения» as deferred, gated on the source being re-enabled and its parser rewritten. If it stays, the spec must say how AC1/AC2/AC3 are verified for it given the source produces no articles, and must state the `blocks = []` vs `blocks = None` answer for its legitimate empty-body outcome.

findings.issue: Declared size M does not match the actual scope, and the feature bundles work that should ship separately. Actual surface: a new shared walker module extracted from orangetrack (which itself carries 94 regression tests), three body-parser rewrites, an autoevolution runs upgrade, a fix in `_llm_common` for the asterisk leak, six exact-equality test assertions to update, six subtitle-lift assertions, plus preview/publisher verification. That is «new architecture» territory (L), not «several components» (M). Separately, the four sources are not one unit: autoevolution is a small swap, t-hunted and lamley are genuinely coupled by the lift trap, and mattel is dead weight.
findings.why_matters: The `**` leak (AC4) is the operator's actual complaint from the live 2026-07-28 publication. Code research traces it to a single root cause (the `**`-markers section of the system prompt is appended unconditionally at `_llm_common.py:123-125`, and no decode ever runs when the article has no blocks) with a single-point fix location. Bundling it behind three parser rewrites leaves a visible, user-facing defect in prod for the entire duration of the feature — even though the spec has already established the opposite precedent by shipping hotfix a509722 first for exactly this reasoning.
findings.fix: Either re-label as L, or split: (1) hotfix now — the `**` leak, AC4 only, shippable today outside the window; (2) shared walker extraction + autoevolution; (3) t-hunted + lamley (the lift trap, AC2/AC3/AC10) as the feature proper; (4) mattel deferred. Each increment is independently deliverable and independently verifiable by the операторская сверка.

findings.issue:
Risk 2's mitigation is unachievable as worded, and it covers only half the problem. The double-space join is already fixed (hotfix a509722 routed four call sites through `_text_from_runs`), so that half is done. The unaddressed half is that the walker deliberately eliminates the nested-tag duplication the current flat parsers produce: `Tag.find_all` is recursive, so `

  • …

    • ` and `

    …

    ` each emit their text TWICE today (verified in code research §3.4). The flat text for t-hunted/lamley/mattel will therefore get materially shorter on any post containing lists or blockquotes. Risk 2 promises «интеграционные тесты проверяют, что фильтры видят тот же текст» — the text is intentionally not the same, so that test cannot be written.
findings.why_matters: Three consumers read that flat text and can change verdict: `_is_promo_article` (scans the first 8 paragraphs / 2000 chars — shifting content shifts which markers fall inside the window), `model_extractor.extract_fingerprint` (dedup; fail-open, so harmless), and `_is_text_only_checklist`, which drops the article BEFORE it enters `pending_articles` when the title matches /checklist/ AND total paragraph text is under `_CHECKLIST_BODY_TEXT_FLOOR = 500`. Shorter text moves articles toward that floor, so an article can now be silently discarded that used to publish — with no alert, since the drop is a normal intake decision.
findings.fix: Reword Risk 2 to state the truth — the flat text CHANGES for posts with lists or blockquotes, because duplicates disappear — and replace the impossible mitigation with a real one: the integration tests must assert that the promo filter, the content gate and the checklist gate reach the same VERDICT on representative real articles (not that they see the same text). Add the checklist-floor drop to the risk list explicitly.

findings.issue: Giving three more sources `blocks` puts them on a second LLM call per article, and the spec never mentions the cost or latency. Verified in code research §5.4: all four engines run a variant-B branch guarded by `if expected_block_count and not parsed.get("blocks")`, which fires `_translate_block_strings` — a second model call — whenever the article carries blocks and the model returns no usable blocks list. The JSON envelope explicitly forbids the model from returning a `blocks` field, so this branch is the normal case, not the exception. Related: each engine defines its own local `_PATCHED_TEXT_BLOCK_TYPES` WITHOUT `list_item` (claude 159, gemini 132, openai 129, openrouter 217), diverging from the 4-tuple in `_llm_common.py:115` — so every `list_item` produced for AC3 gets its already-Russian text re-sent to the second-pass translator.
findings.why_matters: Per-article LLM cost and wall-clock latency roughly double for t-hunted, lamley and autoevolution, inside publish slots that already have to complete on schedule. AC3 (lists) makes it worse rather than better, because list_items are the block type the engines forget to skip. None of this appears in «Ограничения» or «Риски», so the operator meets it as a bill and as slower slots.
findings.fix: Add the operational cost to «Ограничения»: «фича переводит эти источники на второй вызов LLM на статью». Decide in the spec whether `list_item` is added to the engines' local patchable-type lists (it should be — it removes the double translation and the RU-degradation risk on list items) and record it as a technical decision.

findings.issue: The heading heuristic in AC2 has no decision boundary. «Короткий» carries no threshold, so the rule cannot be implemented or verified as written, and the implementer will invent a number that directly determines what subscribers see. The rule's interaction with real heading tags is also unstated: t-hunted and lamley already surface `<h2>/<h3>/<h4>` through the current parser and the walker will emit real `heading` blocks for them, so the bold heuristic is a FALLBACK for blogs that fake headings with bold — but the spec presents bold detection as the primary mechanism.
findings.why_matters: The heuristic itself is the right level of ambition — three cheap conditions, cosmetic and reversible failure mode, no ML, no config. But the boundary is where it breaks: a bold sentence ending in «!» is promoted to a heading while the operator's own motivating example ends in «?» and must be promoted, so terminal punctuation alone does not separate them, and the length threshold is doing all the real work. Left unstated, AC2 is unfalsifiable and the operator's сверка cannot say whether a given promotion is a bug or the rule working.
findings.fix:
State the threshold in the spec as a product decision (character count or word count), and state the precedence rule: a real `

/

/

` tag always wins and produces a heading regardless of bold; the bold heuristic applies only to `

` elements. Add the terminal-punctuation set that blocks promotion («.» yes; «?» and «:» do not block, per the motivating example).

findings.issue: The spec's primary success criterion — «взять 3–5 свежих статей с каждого источника, оригинал и Telegraph рядом» — is partly unexecutable against the real sources. mattel is disabled and has produced zero Hot Wheels articles ever, so it yields nothing to compare. lamley is rate-limited to one request per 20 seconds with a 24 h per-URL blacklist and a 1 h process cool-down after five consecutive 429s (lamley_source.py:101, 105-137). autoevolution sits behind bot protection, which the spec itself cites as the reason E2E tests are out of scope.
findings.why_matters: The spec declares this manual сверка to be the substitute for E2E testing («роль E2E выполняет ручная приёмочная сверка») and «единственная проверка, которая ловит расхождение вкуса». If it cannot actually be run for two of the four sources, the feature ships with no acceptance signal for half its scope.
findings.fix: Make «Как проверить / Пользователь проверяет» executable: drop mattel from it (or from the feature), and for lamley/autoevolution state that the сверка uses articles the bot has already fetched and published rather than fresh live requests. If the operator is expected to open the source pages manually in a browser, say so — that side-steps the parser's rate limits entirely and is what actually happens.

findings.issue: The archived `hw_review` CLI stops accepting rows from these sources and the spec does not record the consequence. Once EN rows carry `blocks`, the parity gate at `hw_review.py:396-404` rejects staging with «ru_blocks required (EN has blocks)», and `_validate_block` (300-320) rejects `runs` as an unknown key and `list_item` as an unknown type outright — so the required `ru_blocks` can never be produced for these articles.
findings.why_matters: The spec decides not to revive hw_review, which is fine — it has been archived since 2026-04-30 and is not deployed. But the decision as written («не оживлять») understates what happens: the path does not merely stay archived, it becomes actively unusable as an emergency manual fallback for four of the five sources. If the operator ever reaches for it during an incident, it fails at the staging step.
findings.fix: Add one line to «Технические решения»: after this feature `hw_review stage` cannot process t-hunted/lamley/autoevolution (and mattel) rows at all — the manual path is not just archived but closed for these sources, and this is accepted.

findings.issue: AC11 («предпросмотр показывает форматирование, а не съедает выделенные слова») and the related constraint about the preview allowlist are already satisfied. Hotfix a509722 added `strong`, `u`, `s` to `preview_renderer._ALLOWED_TAGS` (verified at preview_renderer.py:58-62) together with a guard test that the preview allowlist covers every format tag the publisher can emit.
findings.why_matters: Carrying delivered work as an open AC inflates the apparent scope and risks someone re-doing it. It is now a regression guard, not new work.
findings.fix: Reword AC11 as a no-regression criterion and move the preview-allowlist constraint into the «Риски» mitigation column alongside the other two hotfix items, so the remaining scope reads accurately.

findings.issue: `news_bot._strip_plugs_in_blocks` drops a block whose text was emptied by plug-stripping only for types `('paragraph', 'lead', 'heading')` (verified at news_bot.py:1275-1279) — `list_item` is absent, while the RU boilerplate re-filter forty lines later at 3172 does include it. AC3 puts three more sources on the list_item path.
findings.why_matters: A list item whose entire text was a plug survives as an empty block and renders as a bare «• » paragraph on the published page — `_build_content_from_blocks` prepends the bullet unconditionally. Pre-existing (orangetrack has the same hole) but currently rare; AC3 multiplies the exposure.
findings.fix: Add `list_item` to the empty-block drop in the spec's «Как должно работать» step 3, or note it as a known cosmetic defect explicitly accepted.

findings.issue: A new shared module has a deploy-time trap. Prod is Docker with `COPY . .`, so the container is safe, but the legacy rsync path still enumerates modules by name in three FILES arrays (`deploy.sh`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `.github/workflows/deploy_test.yml`) and `tests/test_deploy_files_invariant.py` exists precisely because omitting one causes an ImportError on the next tick with no CI signal. That test asserts specific filenames only, so a NEW module missing from the arrays passes CI silently.
findings.why_matters: Low probability given the Docker path, but the failure mode is total (the bot cannot import and stops publishing) and it is invisible until the next tick.
findings.fix: Add one line to «Ограничения»: a new shared module must be added to the three deploy FILES arrays and to `tests/test_deploy_files_invariant.py`, or the spec should state that the rsync deploy path is dead and the invariant test is legacy.

summary: The idea is sound, well-grounded in real code, and the pre-feature hotfix (a509722) genuinely landed — but the spec under-specifies the production edges: no runtime guard for the alignment invariant it names as its main trap, no decision about image placement or the image cap that the blocks path silently changes on every post, an unresolvable AC4/AC5/AC6 conflict on the fail-open path, and no way to roll back inside the publish window. Scope should also be trimmed and split: mattel is dead weight, and the asterisk fix — the operator's actual complaint — is a small independent hotfix being held behind three parser rewrites.
